main_text.p: qui tamen an fint fubftantia corporea vel incorporea, nondum percipio: quamvis fi per illos primigenea illa, quæ in partibus folidis noftri corporis, atque in ipfo fanguine ineffe dicitur, fubftantia intelligenda fit, quæ nempe ad confimilem fibi fubftantiam fympa-theia quàdam feratur, (quod videtur velle innuere,) corporeos effe neceffe fit; (unde & illi non femel partes tri-buit Papinius, ipfamque illam primi-geniam fanguinis fubftantiam corpori unde profluxit reaffundi poffe ftatuit, vel fecundum totam fubftantiam, vel fe-cundum magis potentem & efficacem illius partem;) at dum pro forma fubftantiali cenfentur habendi, videntur effe in-corporei, cum alias daretur penetra-tio dimenfionum. Audio porrò dari fubftantiam aliquam mediam, quæ à cor-porea mole libera fit, adeoque fit fub-ftantia fpiritualis feu incorporea; at quæ interim omnia replet, adeoque tri-nam dimenfionem habeat, fitque cor-porea;

page.notes: Page number "162" is read from the printed head ("1o2" in the scan, read as 162); uncertain. Several words in the Latin are set in italics as shown; the bracketed phrases were taken as printed. Running head "De Pulvere" set in spaced capitals.
